jp: 木村[きむら]さんは聞[き]き上手[じょうず]で、とても話[はな]し{やすい|pt-yasui}人[ひと]です。
en: Mr. Kimura is a good listener and very easy to talk to.
why: A good listener is easy to talk to, so the verb stem takes やすい.

jp: 友達[ともだち]は気持[きも]ちが顔[かお]に出[で]{やすい|pt-yasui}ので、うそがすぐ分[わ]かります。
en: My friend's feelings show easily on their face, so I can spot a lie right away.
why: Feelings that show easily on the face take 〜やすい; にくい would make the lie hard to spot.

jp: 旅行[りょこう]の予定[よてい]は変[か]わり{やすい|pt-yasui}ので、ホテルは前日[ぜんじつ]まで取[と]り消[け]せる所[ところ]にしました。
en: Travel plans change easily, so I chose a hotel I can cancel until the day before.
why: Choosing a cancellable hotel only makes sense if plans tend to change: 変わりやすい.

jp: 駅[えき]の前[まえ]の店[みせ]なら場所[ばしょ]が分[わ]かり{やすい|pt-yasui}ので、待[ま]ち合[あ]わせにいいです。
en: A shop in front of the station is easy to find, so it is good for meeting up.
why: A good meeting place is one that is easy to find: 分かりやすい.

jp: 人前[ひとまえ]で緊張[きんちょう]し{やすい|pt-yasui}性格[せいかく]なので、発表[はっぴょう]の前[まえ]の晩[ばん]はいつも眠[ねむ]れません。
en: I am the kind of person who gets nervous easily in front of others, so I can never sleep the night before a presentation.
why: A personality tendency to do something easily is 〜やすい.

jp: このグループは意見[いけん]を言[い]い{やすい|pt-yasui}雰囲気[ふんいき]があって、会議[かいぎ]が楽[たの]しいです。
en: This group has an atmosphere where it is easy to voice opinions, so the meetings are fun.
why: A friendly atmosphere makes opinions easy to voice, hence 言いやすい.

jp: 兄[あに]は感動[かんどう]し{やすい|pt-yasui}人[ひと]で、映画[えいが]を見[み]ると、すぐ泣[な]きます。
en: My older brother is easily moved and cries as soon as he watches a film.
why: Someone who cries at once is easily moved: 感動しやすい.

jp: 昨日[きのう]の会議[かいぎ]は、資料[しりょう]が見[み]{やすくて|pt-yasui}、よく分[わ]かりました。
en: Yesterday's meeting had easy-to-read documents, so I understood well.
why: Readable documents explain why understanding was good; 見やすくて joins the clauses.

jp: このアンケートは短[みじか]くて答[こた]え{やすい|pt-yasui}ので、みんな協力[きょうりょく]してくれると思[おも]います。
en: This questionnaire is short and easy to answer, so I think everyone will cooperate.
why: Being easy to answer is the reason people will cooperate: 答えやすい.

jp: 旅行[りょこう]の日程[にってい]は、少[すこ]し余裕[よゆう]があるほうが動[うご]き{やすい|pt-yasui}と思[おも]います。
en: I think a travel schedule with some slack is easier to move around in.
why: Slack in the schedule makes moving around easier: 動きやすい.

jp: 山田[やまだ]さんの字[じ]は丁寧[ていねい]で、読[よ]み{やすかった|pt-yasui}です。
en: Mr. Yamada's handwriting was neat and easy to read.
why: Neat handwriting is easy to read; the past of 〜やすい is やすかった.

jp: 親友[しんゆう]を悲[かな]しませたくなくて、悪[わる]い知[し]らせは言[い]い{にくい/づらい|pt-yasui}です。
en: I don't want to make my best friend sad, so bad news is hard to tell.
why: Not wanting to hurt a friend makes the news hard to say: 言いにくい.

jp: 彼女[かのじょ]は無口[むくち]で、近[ちか]づき{にくい/づらい|pt-yasui}人[ひと]です。
en: She is quiet and a person who is hard to approach.
why: A quiet person is hard to get close to: 近づきにくい.

jp: 悩[なや]みがあるときは、友達[ともだち]にも相談[そうだん]し{にくい/づらい|pt-yasui}ものです。
en: When you have worries, they are hard to talk over even with friends.
why: The sentence says consulting is hard, so 〜にくい, not the easy or wanting forms.

jp: 初[はじ]めて会[あ]う人[ひと]の前[まえ]では、本当[ほんとう]の気持[きも]ちが話[はな]し{にくい/づらい|pt-yasui}です。
en: In front of people I am meeting for the first time, it is hard to speak my real feelings.
why: Hesitation in front of strangers makes speaking hard: 話しにくい.

jp: 天気予報[てんきよほう]が当[あ]たらない季節[きせつ]は、旅行[りょこう]の計画[けいかく]が立[た]て{にくい/づらい|pt-yasui}です。
en: In seasons when the weather forecast is unreliable, it is hard to make travel plans.
why: Unreliable forecasts make planning difficult: 立てにくい.

jp: 先輩[せんぱい]の意見[いけん]は正[ただ]しいので、反対[はんたい]し{にくい/づらい|pt-yasui}です。
en: My senior's opinion is correct, so it is hard to oppose it.
why: Because the opinion is correct, opposing it is hard: 反対しにくい.

jp: 喧嘩[けんか]したあとは、自分[じぶん]から謝[あやま]り{にくい/づらい|pt-yasui}ものです。
en: After a quarrel, it is hard to be the first to apologise.
why: Pride makes being the first to apologise hard: 謝りにくい.

jp: 手帳[てちょう]は小[ちい]さくて、予定[よてい]が書[か]き{にくい/づらい|pt-yasui}です。
en: My planner is small, so it is hard to write my plans in it.
why: A small planner makes writing difficult: 書きにくい.

jp: 彼[かれ]のジョークは、意味[いみ]が分[わ]かり{にくくて/づらくて|pt-yasui}、だれも笑[わら]いませんでした。
en: His joke was hard to understand, so nobody laughed.
why: Nobody laughed because the meaning was hard to grasp: 分かりにくくて.

jp: 彼[かれ]は気持[きも]ちを言葉[ことば]にし{にくい/づらい|pt-yasui}タイプで、友達[ともだち]もよく心配[しんぱい]しています。
en: He is the type who finds it hard to put feelings into words, and his friends often worry about him.
why: Friends worry because he is the kind who finds expressing feelings hard: 言葉にしにくい.
